teams.heading: Fiji slip to three straight defeats following home loss against Scotland
teams.body: In their last five matches, Fiji have registered only one victory. They have suffered four defeats across that same span. This slump has left the national side on a current run of three straight defeats. In their most recent fixture in July 2026, the Flying Fijians suffered a 33-17 home loss against Scotland during the Nations Championship group stage.

teams.heading: Ben Spencer undergoes shoulder surgery to leave November availability in doubt
teams.body: Bath have confirmed that scrum-half Ben Spencer has undergone shoulder surgery to resolve a long-standing issue, making him a major doubt for England's matches in November. The 34-year-old will miss the start of the Premiership season and face a tight race to prove his fitness before the Tests against Australia, Japan, and New Zealand. With Spencer sidelined, Steve Borthwick must look down his depth chart behind preferred playmakers Alex Mitchell and Jack van Poortvliet, potentially opening the door for Archie McParland or Raffi Quirke.

lead.why: The news of Ben Spencer's shoulder surgery presents a concrete injury blow that directly impacts England's scrum-half depth ahead of the November internationals.

teams.heading: France held the world number one ranking for only one week
teams.body: France have historically struggled to maintain their position at the very peak of the World Rugby rankings. In the history of the global rankings, the longest unbroken spell France have spent at No. 1 is only one week. This brief stint at the top of the world standings occurred during the window of July 2022 to July 2022.

teams.heading: Ireland playmaker Jack Crowley ruled out until new year with vascular injury
teams.body: Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley has been ruled out until the new year, meaning he will miss November's block of international fixtures. The 26-year-old, who has earned 35 caps since his 2022 debut, has been sidelined since April with a lower limb vascular injury. After sitting out July's matches, Crowley's extended absence rules him out of upcoming Dublin tests against Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan confirmed that "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority" as the playmaker continues his recovery.

lead.why: Jack Crowley being ruled out until the new year is a major injury blow for Ireland ahead of their autumn internationals.

The Azzurri also conceded an average of 28.9 points per match during that run. teams.heading: Francisco Moreno signs for Newcastle Red Bulls after making Argentina debut
teams.body: Argentina tight-head prop Francisco Moreno has signed a one-year contract with Premiership side Newcastle Red Bulls. The 24-year-old, who weighs 143kg, made his international debut against South Africa in Buenos Aires earlier this month. Moreno will join fellow Pumas Franco Molina and Simón Benítez Cruz on Tyneside after his international commitments. He is currently with Felipe Contepomi’s squad preparing for Saturday's opening Test against Australia in San Salvador de Jujuy.

lead.why: The signing of newly capped Pumas prop Francisco Moreno by Premiership side Newcastle Red Bulls is a major international club move for a rising front-row talent.

teams.heading: Allan Alaalatoa named Wallabies captain as Les Kiss rotates Harry Wilson
teams.body: Allan Alaalatoa will captain Australia for the seventh time on Saturday in Salvador de Jujuy after head coach Les Kiss opted to rotate regular skipper Harry Wilson out of the matchday 23. Loosehead prop Isaac Kailea earns a starting spot in a brand-new front row alongside hooker Brandon Paenga-Amosa, while Fraser McReight returns at openside flanker. Kiss highlighted the need to manage a long season, balancing player workloads with the physical demands of facing Argentina on their home turf.

lead.why: The Wallabies have named their matchday squad for the Argentina Test, featuring a change in captaincy and key pack rotations.

teams.heading: Anton Segner ruled out of South Africa tour following ankle surgery
teams.body: Anton Segner will play no further part in the South African tour after undergoing keyhole surgery to treat an infected ankle. The German-born flanker, who impressed on his July debut, becomes the fifth All Black ruled out of the series, joining the likes of Caleb Clarke and Billy Proctor. While Segner will remain with the squad, coach Dave Rennie confirmed he will not summon a replacement for Saturday’s second test in Cape Town, citing sufficient depth in the loose forwards.

lead.why: The tour-ending injury to Anton Segner is the most significant squad update and the primary story across New Zealand coverage today.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus recalls Handré Pollard to start as Springboks target All Blacks
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has recalled Handré Pollard to the starting XV for Saturday’s second Test in Cape Town, benching Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu following the 33-16 loss at Ellis Park. Former fly-half Joel Stransky expressed concern that the selection signals a retreat from the "running game" towards a more conservative approach. The Springboks surrendered their No. 1 world ranking with the Johannesburg defeat but can reclaim top spot with any victory this weekend. John Smit urged the camp to remain calm, noting the Boks "haven’t become a s**t team in one day."

lead.why: The tactical shift of starting Handré Pollard over Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu for the second All Blacks Test is the primary focus of today's rugby coverage.
